The Story of the Woman Who Confessed Her Sins

I bow to Lord Jina, worshipped by gods of all four types, and I write the story of a woman who, through confession of her sinful deeds, attained a good result.

King Vishakhadatt of Banaras had a queen named Kanakprabha. In their service lived a painter named Vichitr, who was very skilled in the art of painting. The painter's wife was called Vichitrpataka, and they had a daughter named Buddhimati. Buddhimati was very beautiful and clever.

One day, Vichitr the painter was painting in the king's special palace, which was very beautiful. His daughter Buddhimati brought food for him. In playfulness, she painted a picture of a peacock's feather on the wall. The painting was so beautiful that no one could tell it was a painting at first glance. Everyone who saw it would say, "That is a peacock's feather." At that very moment, King Vishakhadatt came that way. Seeing the feather, he thought it was real and reached out to pick it up. Seeing this, Buddhimati thought, "The king is foolish. Otherwise, he would not be so deceived."

The next day, Buddhimati showed the king another amazing painting and called out to her father, "Father, come quickly! The youth of the meal-time is passing." Hearing these words, the king was greatly astonished. Not understanding her meaning, he stood staring at her face. Seeing that the king did not understand her meaning, Buddhimati became even more convinced of his foolishness.

This time, Buddhimati tried something else. She hung two curtains on a wall and, under the pretext of showing the king a painting, lifted one curtain. There was no painting behind it. Then the king, hoping to see a painting, stared eagerly at the second curtain. Buddhimati lifted the second curtain too. Not seeing any painting, the king was deeply embarrassed. Seeing his reactions, Buddhimati understood him to be a complete fool and laughed a little. The king was even more astonished. He could not understand Buddhimati's intention at all. He anxiously asked her the reason for her behaviour.

From Buddhimati's reply, he understood that she desired him, and that she had expressed her feelings toward him through sarcasm when calling her father for a meal. The king was already captivated by her beauty, and through her words, his desire grew even stronger. He arranged to meet her in secret.

But after their meeting, Buddhimati's conscience troubled her. She realised that she had committed a grave sin by deceiving the king and indulging in an illicit relationship. Overcome with remorse, she went to a Jain monk and confessed her sins. The monk taught her the path of repentance and purification. Through sincere confession and dedicated spiritual practice, Buddhimati purified her soul and attained a heavenly birth.

This story teaches that confession of sins is a powerful means of purification. Buddhimati, though she had committed a grave sin, through sincere repentance and confession to a monk, was able to purify her soul and attain a better destiny. The wise should never hesitate to confess their sins and seek guidance on the path of righteousness.
